summary: Return the element that appears more than n/2 times (guaranteed to exist).
mainInsight: Because the majority element occupies more than half of the array, it survives pairwise cancellation against all other values: Boyer-Moore voting finds it in one pass with O(1) space.

promptVariants: Which algorithm finds the majority element in O(n) time and O(1) space?
What named technique solves Majority Element optimally?
cards.explanation: Pairing off different elements cannot eliminate a value that occurs more than n/2 times.

incorrectOptionExplanations.Heap of size k: Would work for top-k but costs O(n log k) and extra space.

promptVariants: Why does sorting put the majority element at index n // 2?
Explain why the middle element of the sorted array is the majority.
cards.answer: The majority element occupies more than half of the positions. In sorted order its block of > n/2 equal elements must cover the middle index, whichever end it starts from.
cards.explanation: That is why your sorted solution is correct.

promptVariants: Why does cancelling pairs of different elements preserve the majority?
cards.answer: Remove pairs of distinct elements: each removal takes away at most one copy of the majority element and one non-majority element, so a majority (> n/2) stays a majority of what remains. The counter tracks the surplus of the current candidate.
cards.explanation: Requires the guarantee that a majority exists.

promptVariants: Compare the space and time of the three solutions you know.
Which Majority Element approach is best on both time and space, and how do the others compare?
cards.answer: Hash map: O(n)/O(n). Sort: O(n log n)/O(1) (in place, mutates). Boyer-Moore: O(n)/O(1) - best on both.

promptVariants: When is Boyer-Moore's candidate not guaranteed to be correct?
What assumption does Boyer-Moore rely on?
options: When no element has a count > n/2 (needs a verification pass)
When the array contains negative numbers or zeros mixed in
When n is odd, so that no tie between counts is possible
When some values in the array are repeated many times
cards.answer: When no element has a count > n/2 (needs a verification pass)
cards.explanation: The algorithm only returns the right answer if a majority exists; otherwise verify the candidate with a counting pass.

incorrectOptionExplanations.When the array contains negative numbers: Values are compared only for equality.

promptVariants: Your accepted solution sorts in place. What are its side effects and what is the one-pass alternative?
What are the drawbacks of sorting nums in place for Majority Element, and what is the optimal alternative?
cards.answer: It mutates the caller's array and costs O(n log n). The one-pass O(1)-space alternative is Boyer-Moore: candidate/count voting. (Also prefer `len(nums) // 2` to avoid float conversion.)
cards.explanation: Use sorting when it is the simplest correct answer; mention Boyer-Moore as the optimum.
